primary_sources: Equal Rights Amendment ratification record, 1972-1982 (Congress, March 22, 1972; Indiana, 35th state, 1977)

source: original; stimulus table compiled from the Equal Rights Amendment ratification record

stimulus.source_note: Table compiled from the ratification record: Congress proposed the ERA March 22, 1972; Indiana was the 35th and last state to ratify, in 1977; the deadline was extended to June 30, 1982. Account drawn from the grounding books (Barron's Ch. 10, Topic 8.14; 5 Steps Ch. 27; Princeton Ch. 12).
stimulus.text:
Equal Rights Amendment ratifications (Congress sent the amendment to the states on March 22, 1972; 38 states were needed):

| Year | States ratifying that year | Total ratified |
| 1972 | 22 | 22 |
| 1973 | 8 | 30 |
| 1974 | 3 | 33 |
| 1975 | 1 | 34 |
| 1976 | 0 | 34 |
| 1977 | 1 (Indiana) | 35 |
| 1978-1982 | 0 | 35 |

Congress extended the deadline to June 30, 1982. The amendment fell three states short.

stem: What does the table best show about the ERA's momentum?

options.text: States ratified the amendment at a steady pace every single year.
options.misconception: The table shows 22 ratifications in 1972 and none in 1976, so the pace was not steady.

options.text: No state at all ratified the amendment before 1977.
options.misconception: The table shows 22 states ratifying in 1972 alone.

options.text: Ratification rushed ahead in 1972 and 1973, then nearly stopped.
All 38 states had ratified the amendment by 1974.
options.misconception: The table shows only 33 states by the end of 1974, and 35 in all.

rationales.A: The table shows 22 ratifications in 1972 and none in 1976, so the pace was not steady.
rationales.B: The table shows 22 states ratifying in 1972 alone.
rationales.C: The table gives 30 states by the end of 1973, then only 5 more in the next nine years.
rationales.D: The table shows only 33 states by the end of 1974, and 35 in all.
rationales.general:
1. Read the totals down the column in order: 22, then 30, then 33, 34, 34, and 35.
2. The big jumps come in 1972 and 1973, and the years after that add almost nothing.
3. So the amendment rushed ahead first, then nearly stopped.
Remember: Totals that climb fast and then flatten tell a clear story of momentum lost.
